newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government wins confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian government wins confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won a vote of confidence in parliament on Wednesday, its second within a week, to ram through a decree covering development projects.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi called the vote in the lower house to sweep aside some 300 amendments to the draft bill proposed by the separatist Northern League party which had been blocking its passage into law for months.

The vote in the Chamber of Deputies, where Prodi depends on the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for support, was carried by 312 to 267, officials said. If a government loses a confidence motion it must resign.

Prodi's centre-left government faces a legislative nightmare following a recent Constitutional Court ruling which banned his cabinet from continuing the traditional practice of re-issuing expiring draft government laws.

The government called a confidence vote last Wednesday on another decree covering a bank rescue plan, which was about to expire. In all, almost 20 further decrees are due to expire soon and a government minister said that, if necessary, confidence votes would be used to push all of them into law.
The main centre-right opposition bloc, led by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, denounced the tactic, saying the government was ignoring valid objections to the draft laws.
